title: CCTC Compliance Metadata
description: Machine-readable regulatory metadata for a CCTC repository. Authoritative source: CCTC-team/compliance-engine.

schema_version.description: Schema version of this metadata. An integer >= 1; the validator workflow declares which versions it accepts via its supported_schema_versions input. The current schema is version 1 — the single initial version, which already includes validated_paths/exempt_paths and ctq_factors/governing_documents. Bumped only on a future breaking change.

regulatory_tier.description: Inspection bucket and validation rigour. Must match the org custom property `regulatory_tier` set on this repo.

regulatory_pillars.description: Which regulatory clusters apply to this repo. Each pillar bundles a set of related regulations — the granular citation register lives in the CTU's QMS / SOPs, not here. An inspector wants to see that you considered each pillar (including the ones you ruled out), not that you enumerated every paragraph of every regulation.

pillar.description:
Allowed pillars and what they bundle:
- uk-statutory — UK law baseline: UK CT Regs 2004 (as amended by SI 2025/538), UK-GDPR, DPA 2018, NHS-DSPT, HRA Transparency, CAG-S251 (conditional on unconsented PID). Mandatory for any UK trial work.
- mhra-csv-di — MHRA audit focus: ICH E6 (R3), MHRA GxP Data Integrity Guidance, MHRA Inspectorate CSV-for-GCP expectations. How the system is built and validated.
- infra-security — Hosting environment: Cyber Essentials Plus, ISO 27001. Frequently a contractual gate for NIHR/UKRI-funded work.
- international-ehr-standards — 21 CFR Part 11 and EU Annex 11. Applies only with FDA/EMA submission exposure; out-of-scope for UK-only academic trials.
- eu-ct-regulation — EU CTR 536/2014. Applies only when the trial has active EU sites (CTIS-routed since Jan 2025).
- samd-aimd — MHRA Software/AI as Medical Device. Applies only when the system makes or guides clinical decisions (e.g. dose-adjustment algorithms). A pure data-capture EDC is not SaMD.

notes.description: Optional rationale or scoping detail. Useful when status is `out-of-scope` (so an inspector can see you considered and ruled out) or `partial` (which sub-areas are in scope).

gamp_category.description: GAMP 5 software category. 3 = off-the-shelf unconfigured, 4 = configured (e.g. RAVE/REDCap as deployed), 5 = custom code (in-house apps, scripts, EMs).

retention_years.description: Minimum retention period in years for data/code held by this system. UK CT Regs (as amended by SI 2025/538, in force 28 April 2026) require 25 years for trial records on applications submitted on or after that date; pre-amendment trials remain on the 5-year rule under the 2004 Regs.

audit_trail_kind.description: Inspector-readiness: what kind of audit trail this system provides. MHRA Inspectorate expects extractable, immutable trails for gcp-critical systems.

account_model.description: Inspector-readiness: are user accounts individually attributable? MHRA position is that shared accounts break ALCOA+ attributability for any GCP-relevant action.

pid_boundary.description: Inspector-readiness: where is patient-identifiable data held relative to this system? `separated` = system holds only pseudonymised/coded data; `commingled` = system holds direct PID; `none` = system handles no PID at all.

csv_evidence.description: Inspector-readiness: URL or repo path to the Computer System Validation evidence pack (URS/FS/IQ/OQ/PQ + risk assessment). Critical-trial GAMP 5 systems must be able to point at this on demand.

last_reviewed.description: ISO date of the last formal review of this metadata.

review_cadence_months.description: Maximum interval between reviews, in months.

validated_paths.description: Glob patterns (gitignore-style) for paths inside this repo that constitute the validated state. The traceability gate workflow enforces Risk ID + Requirement ID linkage on PRs that change any matching file. If omitted, the gate defaults to strict mode (every PR gated).

exempt_paths.description: Glob patterns for files that sit inside a validated_paths match but are not themselves validated artefacts (typically docs, READMEs, comments-only files). Subtracted from the validated set when computing whether a PR triggers the gate.

release_targets_path.description: Path to this repo's release-targets manifest (the binding between the canonical build-target contract and this repo's build commands; schema: release-targets.schema.json). Optional; the release and compliance-check workflows default to `.github/release-targets.yml` when omitted. Override only if the manifest lives elsewhere.

traceability.description: Requirement -> evidence map for the regulated feature lifecycle, keyed by the card's `Requirement ID` (the foreign key between the project board and this repo). Each entry names the URS document and the executable feature tests that prove that requirement. ProjectV2 custom fields have no list or multi-line text type, so this variable-length mapping lives here — version-controlled and reviewed in the same PR as the `.spec`/`.feature` files it points at — rather than as card free-text. The `vv_tests_pass` precondition resolves `Requirement ID` through this map and asserts each path exists; the board-evidence report (getval v2) embeds the referenced content at the release tag. Optional: a repo whose feature tests do not yet exist may omit it.

urs.description: Repo-relative path to the User Requirement Specification (`.spec`) document for this requirement.

features.description: Repo-relative paths to the executable feature tests (Gherkin `.feature` files) that prove this requirement. At least one.

ctq_factors.description: Critical-to-Quality factors (CCTU/FRM129) this system supports or safeguards. ICH E6(R3) Principle 6 treats fit-for-purpose validation of computerised systems handling clinical data/endpoints as a CtQ factor; this anchors the system to its FRM129 entry so an inspector can trace CtQ factor -> risk -> requirement -> V&V. Required for gcp-critical.

frm129_ref.description: CtQ factor identifier on CCTU/FRM129 (trial-specific form ID + row, e.g. FRM129-XYZ-001#3).

tier.description: FRM129 classification. critical = compromise breaks participant safety / result reliability; important = significant but not critical. 'neither' factors are not listed.

governing_documents.description: QMS documents (SOPs, guidance, forms, templates) governing this system's validation and risk management — the pointer layer between repo controls and the CTU QMS. The granular regulation register stays in the QMS. Required for gcp-critical.

ref.description: QMS document number, e.g. CCTU/SOP040, CCTU/GD073, CCTU/FRM129.

state_lifecycle.description: Data & state lifecycle capability declaration (contract: CCTC-team/compliance-engine docs/data-state-lifecycle-contract.md). Declares which persistent stores this app has and which optional state:* verbs it implements, so the UAT process can (re)build the app's state without knowing its internals. The verb->command binding lives in release-targets.yml; this block declares only the stores and posture. OMIT THIS BLOCK ENTIRELY for an app with no persistent state — that app's UAT data step is a clean no-op and is conformant. The engine-side conformance check asserts every store declared here resolves to mandatory state:* bindings in release-targets.yml.

stores.description: The persistent stores this app maintains. At least one (an app with none omits the whole block). `kind` is INFORMATIONAL — the engine never branches on it; it exists so an inspector and the audit record can see what each store is.

name.description: Free-form store name used as the key in the baseline-version tuple, e.g. identity, graph, messaging.

kind.description: Informational store type, e.g. sql-server, neo4j, rabbitmq, sqlite. Not interpreted by the engine.

synthetic_only.description: Attestation that UAT stores hold ONLY synthetic, non-production data (GxP — never production clinical data in UAT). Must be true.

prod_isolation.description: Attestation that UAT stores run on a server PHYSICALLY SEPARATE from production (Decision 10). The contract-runner fails closed on any destructive verb (rebuild/restore) unless this is true. Logical isolation (a separate database on a shared instance) is NOT sufficient — a mis-scoped teardown on a shared instance can destroy prod.

nonprod_targets.description: Allowlist of UAT host/endpoint identifiers (e.g. uat-db-host:1433) the DESTRUCTIVE state:* verbs (rebuild/restore/teardown) are permitted to act on. prod_isolation:true alone does not authorise a destructive verb: the contract-runner's gate ALSO requires the live target it resolves to match an entry here exactly, and a store that omits this field has destructive verbs DISABLED (fail-closed). Logical isolation (a separate database on a shared instance) is NOT sufficient — the gate rejects a target that shares a host/instance with production. Additive and optional at the schema level so existing repos are unaffected.

capabilities.description: Which OPTIONAL state:* verbs this app implements. The mandatory verbs (migrate/seed/rebuild/verify/baseline-version) are assumed for any declared store. `snapshot` implies state:snapshot + state:restore are bound and lets a store preserve within-cycle tester state across a failed migration; a store without it is rebuilt-from-baseline on failure (within-cycle state lost).

cycle.description: Informational rollover-cadence hint, e.g. per-release, weekly.
